jolly-roger.title: The Jolly Roger (Pirate Flag)

colors.note: Death, darkness, and the pirate's menace.
The skull and crossbones; mortality and defiance.

desc:
- A black field bearing a white skull above two crossed bones (or swords)
- The most famous pirate flag, used from the early 18th century during the Golden Age of Piracy
- Many variants existed — Edward 'Blackbeard' Teach used a skeleton with a spear and bleeding heart; Calico Jack Rackham's had crossed swords instead of bones
- The name 'Jolly Roger' may derive from the French 'joli rouge' (pretty red) or from a general slang term for a grinning skull
- **Construction:** a black field with a white skull and crossbones (or variant device) centred. No standard ratio
trivia:
- No two pirate captains used the same Jolly Roger — each had a personalised version
- The skull and crossbones design conveyed a specific message of danger and death
- Most pirate flags actually used variations of red or solid colours; the black 'Jolly Roger' is more legend than historical fact

white-ensign.title: White Ensign of the Royal Navy

colors.note: Field of the Royal Navy ensign.
The Union Jack in the canton.

desc:
- The White Ensign (St George's Ensign) is the ensign of the Royal Navy, featuring a white field with the red Cross of St George and the Union Jack in the canton
- It has been used by the Royal Navy since 1864 and is one of the most recognisable naval ensigns in the world
- Ships flying this ensign are under the protection of the Crown
- **Construction:** a white field with a red Cross of St George extending to the edges, and the Union Flag occupying the upper-hoist canton. Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- The White Ensign is used by the British Royal Navy
- Features the Union Jack and the cross of St. George
- One of the oldest naval flags still in use

red-ensign.title: Red Ensign of the British Merchant Navy

colors.note: The Union Jack in the canton.

desc: - The Red Ensign (Red Duster) is the civil ensign of the United Kingdom, flown by British merchant ships. Many colonial flags were based on it
- **Construction:** a red field (1:2) with the Union Flag in the upper-hoist canton, occupying one-quarter of the flag area
trivia:
- The Red Ensign is used by various nations and maritime purposes
- Represents British naval and maritime traditions
- Used by merchant marine and civilian ships

signal-flags.title: International Maritime Signal Flags
desc:
- The International Code of Signals uses 26 alphabetical signal flags, 10 numerical pennants, and several special flags to communicate between ships at sea
- Developed from earlier systems dating to the 17th century, the current International Code was adopted in 1857 and revised by the IMO
- Each flag represents a letter and also has a specific meaning when flown individually
- **Construction:** varies by flag
- The signal flags use a standardised set of colours and geometric patterns (stripes, crosses, triangles) for maximum visibility at sea
- Ratio typically 3:4 for rectangular flags
trivia:
- Each International Code signal flag has a single-letter meaning when flown alone
- 'B' (Bravo) means 'I am loading, unloading, or carrying dangerous cargo'
- All 26 letter flags have distinct meanings used in naval and maritime communication
